item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Faith Evans Loses As Judge Awards Biggie’s Mother’s Trust $12.5M
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Faith Evans lost a fight over $12.5 million owed to Voletta Wallace's trust, with a judge also awarding interest on the payouts.
item.content:encoded:
Faith Evans lost a $12.5 million court fight over money owed to Biggie’s late mother’s trust, with a Delaware judge ruling that the trust was entitled to the payouts plus interest.

The October 27 decision set the amount at $12,518,336. The money came from distributions tied to Voletta Wallace’s interest in Notorious B.I.G., LLC, the company Evans manages that holds rights to the late rapper’s intellectual property.

Judge Kathaleen St. J. McCormick of the Delaware Court of Chancery rejected an effort to limit the trust’s payout to $48,612 while a separate family dispute plays out in Pennsylvania.

The key issue was when the trust gained the right to receive money. It was formally admitted as an LLC member months after Wallace’s death, but that delay did not erase its claim to earlier payouts. Judge McCormick wrote:

“The short answers to the remaining questions are that the Trust did not become a member until December 12, 2025, when it executed the instrument required under the LLC Agreement, but the Trust is entitled to distributions made prior to that time in the amount of $12,518,336.”

Wallace died on February 21, 2025. Her will left her estate to the Voletta Wallace Revocable Trust. Wayne Barrow sued Evans on the trust’s behalf after she refused to recognize it as a member of the company.

Evans and Wallace formed the LLC in 2007. Under their later agreement, each assigned half of her distribution rights to Biggie’s children, leaving Wallace, Evans, T’yanna Wallace and Christopher Jordan Wallace each entitled to 25% of the company’s payouts.

The dispute followed Primary Wave’s 2025 deal for a stake in Biggie’s music and related rights. AllHipHop previously covered Barrow’s lawsuit over the withheld proceeds and the trust’s August court victory.

This time, Evans and the company argued that the larger sum should not be paid out while her son, Christopher Jordan Wallace (CJ), challenged Barrow’s authority as sole executor and trustee. They offered to place the disputed funds with the Delaware court instead.

Judge McCormick rejected that proposal and explained why the Pennsylvania challenge did not justify withholding the money:

“The economic rights associated with Ms. Wallace’s units now belong to the Trust. Plaintiff Wayne Barrow, who appears in this action on behalf of the Trust, also holds Letters Testamentary issued on April 21, 2025, making him the sole executor of the Estate. Pennsylvania law provides that ‘[n]o act of administration performed by a personal representative in good faith shall be impeached by the subsequent revocation of his letters or by the subsequent probate of a will, of a later will or of a codicil.’ The outcome of the Pennsylvania action, therefore, will not affect the actions taken by Mr. Barrow related to the Trust, Ms. Wallace’s estate, and the Trust’s entitlement to distributions as of Ms. Wallace’s date of death. I therefore find no need for the accrued distributions to be deposited with the Register in Chancery. They are due to the Trust.”

The decision also added interest to the unpaid distributions, running from the date each payout was made rather than the date of this ruling.

“In sum, the Trust became a member as of December 12, 2025, the date of the Written Consent. The Trust is entitled to distributions made as of the date of Ms. Wallace’s death. The Trust is entitled to prejudgment interest on those distributions, accruing as of the date on which the distribution was made. Prejudgment interest will be at the statutory rate, compounded quarterly.”

Judge McCormick gave Barrow 20 days to submit a final form of order reflecting this decision and the court’s earlier rulings.

item.title: 50 Cent Mocks Tia Kemp’s ‘Gangsta Granny Act’ After Court Victory
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: 50 Cent accuses Tia Kemp of further online misconduct in an Instagram message following temporary court protection for Sire.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent is mocking Tia Kemp’s “Gangsta granny act” after winning a court order protecting his teenage son, Sire.

He shared a screenshot of the injunction coverage and accused Kemp of continuing to target his family and lawyers.

“I know this is not gonna make her stop making antisemitic remarks about my Jewish lawyers, posting revenge porn and attacking a child but it will make her re think her Gangsta granny act. It’s not ok”

The antisemitism and “revenge porn” claims remain the rapper’s allegations, not findings established by the Florida judge. He also tagged several autism-awareness accounts, recalling earlier disputes over unverified claims about Sire’s development.

50 had used a similar nickname earlier, writing: “It’s not ok to bully minors on line, kids have killed them selves over things people have said about them. That gangster granny act is not gonna work no 🏳️ white flags.”

TMZ obtained court documents showing the judge ordered Kemp to remain at least 500 feet from 14-year-old Sire. The injunction also forbids contact through social media and requires Kemp to surrender firearms upon being served.

The feud followed 50’s mockery of an alleged assault on William Roberts III, Kemp’s adult son with Rick Ross. WFTV reported his offer to help the accused attacker, but whether he paid the man’s bond remains unconfirmed.

His official YouTube channel shows Kemp and Ross’ son at Floyd Mayweather’s mansion in a 2009 video.

The earlier court petition accused Kemp of mocking Sire’s development and placing explicit material beside his photo. 50 objected: “This is the greatest example of bullying a minor saying he is on the spectrum. I have friends who kids are, it’s not a joke.”

A separate federal lawsuit seeks at least $6 million over alleged false statements about Sire and his mother, Daphne Joy.

His lawyers wrote in the complaint: “Ms. Kemp shamelessly used the label ‘on the spectrum’ as a pejorative slur hurled at a child to humiliate him and his family.”

Kemp has rejected the rapper’s accusations, saying, “You can’t bully me b***h,” in an earlier social media response.

A November 3 hearing will determine whether to extend the protective restrictions beyond their scheduled expiration that day.

item.title: Queen Latifah Says “The Voice” Battle Cracked Her Ring
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Queen Latifah said a "The Voice" duet cracked her ring, then chose Mia Knight to keep moving through the competition.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Latifah joked that “The Voice” singers owed her a ring after their performance cracked its stone.

The moment came when Mia Knight and Sophia Liano sang “Never Enough” from “The Greatest Showman.” Both singers were on her team, leaving the Hip-Hop star to choose who would stay.

“I literally had to take my ring off because I cracked the stone on here on one of those notes,” she said. She joked that a win on the show could settle the bill.

Knight won the Battle and advanced to Cut Week.

For Latifah, the choice came down to how the young singer handled the microphone and claimed the stage. She praised both contestants, then explained why she wanted to keep working with Knight.

The coach also drew on her own start in music. She noted that Knight was 16 and that her own first record came out when she was 17. She felt the teen was ready for the next round.

Latifah had already pushed hard to work with Knight. During the September 21 season premiere, she turned her chair first as Knight sang Sienna Spiro’s “You Stole The Show.” Riley Green and Clarkson followed, while Adam Levine stayed put.

The new First In button let the first coach claim an artist without waiting for the singer to pick a team. Each coach could use it once. Latifah used hers on Knight, cutting short the competition for the New Jersey singer.

Season 30 marked Latifah’s first turn as a coach on the NBC series, joining Clarkson, Levine and Green. Knight’s next test comes in Cut Week in November.

item.title: Megan Thee Stallion Adds Uncle Waffles To Las Vegas Hottieween Circus
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion added Uncle Waffles to her Las Vegas Hottieween party, which will mix circus flair, costumes and charity.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion added amapiano DJ Uncle Waffles as a special guest to her Hottieween party for this year’s Las Vegas celebration.

Megan announced the booking, and Waffles reposted it on X. “We shutting down Vegas with my Queeen,” Waffles wrote.

The party takes place Friday, October 30, at Zouk Nightclub inside Resorts World Las Vegas. The resort lists the hours as 9 P.M. to 3 A.M. Guests must be at least 21, and costumes are required. That puts the celebration on the night before Halloween, with the party continuing into Saturday morning.

Megan is working with Cirque du Soleil on this year’s circus theme.

The celebration will also feature her Chicas Divertidas tequila, as AllHipHop previously reported. Some of the night’s proceeds will go to her Pete & Thomas Foundation, keeping charity part of the annual event.

The three-part “Hottieween” series cast her as a private investigator in 2019. Dave East joined her on screen, with Teyana Taylor behind the camera as director. That let Megan act out her love of horror as the Halloween tradition grew.

Her costumes have drawn from film, too. She wore a Pinhead costume inspired by “Hellraiser” in 2021. At the 2023 Atlanta party, she became a talking flower in a Tim Burton-inspired setting. GloRilla, Victoria Monét and John Boyega were among the guests that year.

The move to Vegas follows Hottieween stops in Chicago in 2024 and Houston in 2025. Both helped raise money for the foundation. Last year’s Houston edition was a Halloween concert where fans also had to wear costumes.

The foundation’s work reaches women, children, older adults and underserved communities in Houston and beyond. Its programs cover education, housing, health and wellness and community goodwill.

Megan created the nonprofit to honor her parents, Joseph Pete III and Holly Thomas.

Among its education projects, the foundation helped renovate literacy and studio rooms at Youth Education Town in 2024.

The project marked the third annual Megan Thee Stallion Day. More than 50 Hotties volunteered, and the young people received books, journals, podcasting equipment and studio gear.

item.title: A$AP Rocky Creative Director Owns “Shroom Clouds” Credit Failure
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: A$AP Rocky's creative director acknowledged uncredited work as the "Shroom Clouds" production team released its original cut.
item.content:encoded:
A$AP Rocky‘s creative director acknowledged that “Shroom Clouds” used work connected to Cache Bunny without credit, while the video’s original production team released a separate cut to show what it had delivered.

Gallardo took responsibility for failing to review AI assets, according to IndiaTimes, which reproduced his Instagram Story. He said protecting creators and their work fell within his job as creative director at AWGE.

“I want to address the concerns with the SHROOM CLOUDS music video directly. During production, a breakdown in our review process of AI-generated assets resulted in the unattributed use of work associated with @cache_bunny. As a Creative Director, my responsibility is to protect creators, respect their work, and safeguard the integrity of AEW. When shit like this happens, as the creative lead, I have to take accountability,” Gallardo said.

“I have reached out directly to @cache_bunny to start a conversation and resolve this matter appropriately. We are fully open to discussing proper attribution and potential collaboration whenever they are ready to connect,” he added.

He also said the team was willing to discuss credit and a possible collaboration. Director Aisultan Seitov and production company ProdCo addressed another part of the dispute: how the released video differed from their work.

ProdCo said it had finished its original version and handed it to the client in January 2024. The company said that cut did not contain the later AI shots, AI processing or the imagery at the center of the complaint.

The company said later editing and AI changes happened without its knowledge or Seitov’s consent. It also objected to the way its production role was credited.

Seitov and ProdCo released their director’s cut on October 27. ProdCo said the release showed the original collaboration between Seitov and Rocky and marked the end of its involvement with the project.

The original cut listed Rocky and Seitov as directors, with production from ProdCo and North of Now Films. Its effects credits included Mathematic and Silent Studios.

The footage dispute began with a 2019 piece by Cache Bunny and Ari Fararooy, featuring parkour athlete Jason Paul. Paul was filmed on a football field with a 360-degree camera, then Cache Bunny used visual effects to turn the setting into a tunnel.

Cache Bunny accused Rocky’s production of using that work without permission and replacing Paul with the rapper through AI. The artist pointed to matching grass and shadows in the two clips.

AllHipHop previously covered Paul’s response. He questioned how the footage made it into the finished video but said he didn’t blame Rocky personally.

Cache Bunny also asked why the team had not sought a license for the clip or made a new version based on the idea.

item.title: Nelly Books India’s Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Nelly joined Khalid and Swae Lee on the Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival lineup for November 20 and 21 in Meghalaya, India.
item.content:encoded:
Nelly will headline India’s Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival, sharing the bill with Khalid and Swae Lee. The two-day event runs November 20 and 21 at Madan Kurkalang in Bhoirymbong, Meghalaya.

Boys Like Girls and singer Darshan Raval share Nelly’s November 20 opening-day bill, according to India Today NE.

The lineup launch announcement took place at Shillong’s Meghalayan Age Pavilion at Ward’s Lake, with Meghalaya government Commissioner and Secretary Rosetta Mary Kurbah present.

Galantis and British singer Elliot James Reay are also among the international acts announced for the festival.

This year’s theme, “Year of Generations,” splits the weekend between two eras of music. The opening day focuses on millennial and Y2K sounds, while the second day leans toward Gen Z and current music.

That puts Nelly on the bill’s early-2000s side, with a career that earned him three Grammy wins and 12 nominations.

He won for “Hot In Herre” and “Dilemma” at the 2003 awards, then picked up another trophy for “Shake Ya Tailfeather” in 2004. Country Grammar earned a Best Rap Album nomination in 2001, while Nellyville competed for Album Of The Year in 2003.

Jessie Lyngdoh, Gingerfeet, Scribe, W.I.S.H. and Bhayanak Maut are among the Indian and regional performers booked for the festival. Beyond the stages, organizers have announced cosplay, fashion events, beatboxing, eating contests, ziplining and a Ferris wheel.

Meghalaya’s musicians have an industry event before the concerts.

They plan a Music Summit for November 19 in collaboration with India International Music Week. Workshops and discussions are intended to help local artists meet booking agents, label representatives and concert promoters from other countries.

The new booking comes as television viewers are set to see more of the demands of his touring life.

Season two of “Nelly and Ashanti: We Belong Together” arrives on Peacock November 19, with his storyline examining the physical toll of years of touring.

item.title: Jennifer Lopez Turns Empty Nest Heartache Into New Music
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jennifer Lopez said her twins' move to college sent her back to the studio, where joy and grief shaped her new music.
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Lopez returned to the studio after her twins left for college, turning their absence into new music.

Speaking with Variety, the singer said Max and Emme’s departure gave her room to write and record again. She described the change as frightening and sad, even as she praised the songs it helped produce.

Her new track, “Proof of Love,” deals with grief and absence over dance music, she said. The hurt can show how much a person matters.

“They take up such a big part of your brain for so long, and when they’re gone, which is devastating and sad and scary, you’re facing a life that’s totally different now, and you’re like, ‘What am I going to do with this space and this time?’ For me, I just went back in the studio. I’ve written some of the best songs that I’ve ever written, and I’m really excited,” Jennifer Lopez said.

She also described the broader music she has been making as joyful, with some sadness still inside it.

The move had been weighing on her well before the twins packed up.

During a May appearance on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” Lopez said she had cried for months while preparing for their high school graduation.

Writing their yearbook messages took two days. The twins planned to attend different colleges, and she supported each of their choices. She joked that small dorm rooms might make them miss home and come back to visit.

Her stage work also carried a hopeful tone earlier this year. AllHipHop covered her Las Vegas residency opening, where she told fans she was learning and growing.

That Caesars Palace production opened December 30, 2025. It mixed her own hits with Broadway songs and featured a 17-piece band. Ja Rule joined the opening performances for “I’m Real” and “Ain’t It Funny.”

The song will be a bonus on the first vinyl edition of her 2011 album Love?, arriving in November. Preorders began October 28, with three versions planned.

Fans will also get “The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas,” a filmed version of the stage production. CBS announced that the March 28 closing performance will air November 26 from 8 to 10 P.M. ET/PT.

Paramount+ will carry an extended version.

The special will include hits, Broadway standards and songs that helped shape her own career. The Thanksgiving slot also ties into a family tradition: Lopez and her relatives gathered to watch movie musicals during the holiday.

item.title: Megan Thee Stallion’s “Thin Ice” Streams Jump 152%
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion saw "Thin Ice" daily U.S. streams rise 152% after taking the Tina Tuesday freestyle beyond YouTube.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion saw daily U.S. on-demand streams for “Thin Ice” rise 152% between October 24 and 26.

According to Billboard’s report on Luminate data, the freestyle drew 98,000 streams Saturday, 174,000 Sunday and 247,000 Monday.

It reached streaming services October 24 after starting on YouTube. The three daily totals added up to about 519,000 streams over that stretch.

“Thin Ice” sampled the intro to Limp Bizkit’s “Break Stuff” and joined her Tina Tuesday freestyle series. The song had not entered the Hot 100 when Billboard reported the increase.

The official performance arrived on Megan’s YouTube channel on October 20 and ran two minutes and 27 seconds.

By October 28, the upload had more than 10.9 million views. That video counter covered a different period from the three days of streaming figures.

Megan told Marie Claire she had spent the summer recording and rewriting Act III after missing her intended summer release window.

Her new music also followed a change in the business behind her releases.

On August 14, Megan announced a partnership with Interscope Records that gave her access to its worldwide distribution and other support while she kept ownership of her masters and publishing.

Her company, Hot Girl Productions, remained home to her music.

She regained that control after a long fight with her former label.

As AllHipHop previously reported, she signed with Carl Crawford’s 1501 Certified Entertainment in 2018 and sued the company in 2020. The two sides settled and separated in October 2023. They did not make the settlement terms public.

Hot Girl Productions had already released “Cobra” in November 2023 when Warner Music Group announced its agreement with Megan in February 2024.

Warner counted “HISS” as her second solo release through her own company. Radio promotion and marketing were among the services available under that deal. She kept control of her recordings, publishing and creative direction.

The agreement also let Megan use Warner’s network for other acts on her imprint.

“I’ve always wanted to create music on my terms while building a legacy that extends beyond the industry,” Megan said in her Interscope announcement.

item.title: Outkast’s Nike Collection Heads To More Stores
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Outkast joined Nike, Class Trip and the University of Georgia for a clothing collection with a wider retail rollout set for October 28.
item.content:encoded:
Outkast teamed with Nike, Class Trip and the University of Georgia to create clothes inspired by the duo’s style, with a wider rollout that started on October 28.

Nike plans to bring the full Outkast U range to nike.com and select stores, following the October 27 launch through SNKRS, Class Trip and Atlanta retailers.

The clothes borrow from André 3000 and Big Boi’s wardrobes. Georgia’s G carries Outkast’s crown, while jerseys bear 96, a nod to the year ATLiens arrived. The duo’s “Roses” video also helped guide the look.

Class Trip founder Brian Francis said André’s recollections of visiting Athens came up over lunch, which gave the project its start.

A red varsity jacket pairs wool with black leather sleeves. It uses chenille patches and chain-stitch embroidery, with Georgia and Outkast lettering across the back. The range also includes rugby shirts, a satin bomber and tees.

“We wanted to create something as timeless as their music,” said Jon Tietz, Class Trip’s creative director.

Class Trip’s store listed the crown snapback at $50 and the “Ms. Jackson” T-shirt at $60. The cotton jersey was $145, and the hoodie was $180.

The partnership follows Outkast’s Waffle House collaboration, which launched through the group’s website on October 2.

That project took a line from Big Boi’s “So Fresh, So Clean” verse and turned it into a Waffle House marquee, connecting the duo’s catalog with another familiar piece of Southern life.

Hip-Hop historian NuFace discussed that earlier pairing in an interview with AllHipHop.

“OutKast has become part of the culture, the identity and the language of Atlanta,” he told AllHipHop about the Waffle House collaboration. No new OutKast music was announced with that partnership.

The connection has roots in the music: André and Big Boi released their debut, Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik, in 1994, then built on it with ATLiens, Aquemini and Stankonia.

Their reach also earned them a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’s 2025 class, with Donald Glover serving as their inductor.

The Hall’s profile traces a sound that drew on funk and jazz as well as rap, part of the range behind that recognition. The Hall counts Outkast among the few Hip-Hop acts to win the Grammy for Album of the Year.

item.title: R. Kelly Finds The Wildest Supporter Who Says Black Community Failed Him
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Iyanla Vanzant sought forgiveness during a wildly candid exchange that said mentorship failed the incarcerated R&B singer.
item.content:encoded:
Iyanla Vanzant Apologized To R. Kelly And Said Community Elders Failed Him

Iyanla Vanzant apologized to R. Kelly on “The Jason Lee Show” over what she described as the Black community’s failure to support him before his imprisonment for sexual abuse.

The author and television personality directed her apology toward the singer while discussing the responsibilities of community elders. Her remarks focused on missed opportunities to address his personal struggles and the people who benefited financially from his career, according to Baller Alert’s account of the interview.

“Forgive me as an elder in our community not being available to support you,” Vanzant said. “Forgive me for ignoring your pain. Forgive me for abandoning you.” 

When host Jason Lee questioned whether she believed she had personally abandoned Kelly, Vanzant expanded her answer to include the broader community.

“Our entire community abandoned him. As an elder, I’m going to own it,” she said.

Vanzant also questioned why people who earned money through Kelly’s success had not done more to help with his reading difficulties. She presented those circumstances as examples of support she believed should have accompanied his commercial achievements. Those assertions represent her assessment of the people surrounding Kelly, rather than findings about what caused his criminal conduct. 

The interview appeared in an Oct. 21 post from Hollywood Unlocked, which described a broader conversation about forgiveness, grief, personal responsibility and celebrity culture. Kelly was among several public figures discussed during the episode.

Her apology comes with a substantial criminal record as its backdrop.

A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Kelly in September 2021 of racketeering and other offenses involving the exploitation of women and children. U.S. District Judge Ann M. Donnelly sentenced him to 30 years in prison in June 2022. Prosecutors said his operation depended on associates who helped facilitate the abuse. 

A separate Chicago jury convicted Kelly in September 2022 of three counts of producing child sexual abuse material and three counts of enticing a minor into sexual activity. He received a 20-year sentence in February 2023, with one year ordered to run consecutively to his New York sentence, producing a combined 31-year term. 

Vanzant’s argument places attention on opportunities she believes were missed before those prosecutions.

The court record establishes another responsibility: Kelly’s own actions toward the women and children he abused. Her appeal for compassion adds to that public conversation without changing the crimes established at trial.
